label: Singularities
notes: Welcome to Arnold's appendix on singularities. The thread we follow is simple to state and deep to develop: when a Lagrangian or Legendrian manifold is projected to physical space, the projection folds, and the fold loci are caustics and wave fronts. The shapes of those folds are not arbitrary; a short, rigid list governs them.

label: Why projections fold
notes: Rays carry a Lagrangian manifold in phase space. Projecting it down to position space is generically a fold, because the manifold is curved while the projection is flat. Where the tangent plane turns vertical the map loses rank, light piles up, and we see a caustic. The whole appendix studies the local form of that loss of rank.

label: Catastrophe of a potential
notes: Each ray system comes from a generating family, a function of one state variable and several parameters. Equilibria are critical points in the state; caustics are where critical points collide as parameters move. So caustic geometry is the bifurcation geometry of a potential, and the elementary catastrophes are exactly the normal forms of those collisions.

label: The fold A_2
notes: The simplest collision is the fold. Two critical points of a cubic generating function approach and annihilate as the control parameter crosses zero. On one side there are two equilibria, on the other none, and the boundary is a single smooth caustic point. This A2 fold is the universal building block of every caustic edge.

label: The cusp A_3
notes: Raise the generating function to quartic and one control parameter is no longer enough; we need two. The discriminant in that control plane is a semicubical cusp, the famous coffee-cup curve. Inside the cusp there are three rays, outside one, and the two fold edges meet tangentially at the sharp point where three critical points coincide.

label: Coffee-cup caustic
notes: Hold a mug under a lamp and the bright curve on the coffee is a real caustic, a cardioid-like nephroid with a cusp. Parallel-ish rays reflect off the circular wall and their envelope concentrates light. This everyday picture is the A3 cusp made visible, and it is structurally stable: jiggle the lamp and the cusp persists.

label: The swallowtail A_4
notes: Wave fronts are Legendrian projections, and their generic singularity in three space is the swallowtail. A quintic generating family produces a self-intersecting folded sheet with two cuspidal edges meeting at a swallowtail point and a curve of transverse self-intersection. It is the A4 member of the same series, one dimension up from the cusp.

label: The A_k series
notes: Folds, cusps and swallowtails are the start of one infinite family. The function x to the k plus one has an A k singularity, and its versal deformation needs k minus one parameters. Caustics in the plane show A2 and A3; wave fronts in space add A4; higher members appear when more parameters are available to unfold them.

label: A-D-E classification
notes: Arnold's theorem says the simple singularities, those with no continuous modulus, fall into exactly three families: A k, D k, and the three exceptionals E6, E7, E8. The same Dynkin diagrams that classify simple Lie algebras and Kleinian surface singularities reappear here. This coincidence is one of the most celebrated patterns in mathematics.

label: Structural stability
notes: Why only this short list? Because a singularity that survives every small perturbation must be one of the simple, finitely determined germs. Thom and Arnold's transversality arguments show that for generic systems only the A-D-E forms occur, and each keeps its shape under deformation. Genericity, not luck, is what makes caustics look the way they do.

label: Maslov index
notes: Each time a ray touches a caustic its phase jumps by a quarter period, and counting these crossings gives the Maslov index. That integer corrects the semiclassical phase and enters the Bohr-Sommerfeld quantization condition. So the fold points we classified geometrically carry the analytic information that turns classical orbits into quantum spectra.

label: Synthesis
notes: Pull the threads together. Lagrangian and Legendrian projections fold; folds are bifurcations of a generating family; their normal forms are the A-D-E simple singularities; structural stability explains why these and no others appear; and the Maslov index reads the fold count back into physics. That is the architecture of Appendix 23.
